title: Input to the `review.findings` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `review.findings`. SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2).

**Unknown keys are refused rather than dropped.** The SDK sets no `extra="forbid"` on the argument model it derives from the handler, so a key it does not recognise is discarded before any Theurian code runs, and a filtered question answered without one of its filters reads as the whole answer (ADR-0031 decision 4). On a filtering tool that is the same defect its own `limit` refuses rather than clamps to avoid.

**Composition.** The context — `projectId`, and the optional `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` — arrives by `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json`. The closure is `unevaluatedProperties: false` and not `additionalProperties: false`, which under a `$ref` composition rejects the very context fields it referenced (ADR-0031 decision 1, measured against `jsonschema` 4.26.0). `projectId` is required by the referent and is not repeated here. `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` are accepted and read by no handler in this build.

**The vocabularies are deliberately not published here as `enum`s.** `reviewer` and `severity` are drawn from closed sets, and `theurian.mcp.findings` records why the rejection stays there: its refusal names every token in the vocabulary, reports an over-long value by its length rather than quoting it, and ends with the omit-the-filter remedy. An `enum` in this file would answer "does not satisfy" in place of all three. The vocabularies are published where a client can read them — `review-findings-response.schema.json` and `docs/protocol/mcp-tools.md` — rather than where a refusal would be worsened by them.

What this file does hold is shape and length: the axes a boundary check can state completely, and the ones that bound the work an untrusted request can ask for before anything is read.

reviewer.description:
Which reviewer's findings to read, as the `Review-Finding:` trailer spells it. One of a closed set of governed tokens; the handler names them all when it refuses, and the historical alias the parser normalises is not accepted as a query (ADR-0029 Amendment 1).

At most 200 characters, the bound every findings filter shares: the longest real value on the other side of these predicates is a 64-character commit sha, so the bound exists to stop a refusal quoting the caller's own bytes back at it rather than to describe the data (#17).

severity.description: Which severity to read, as the trailer writes it — upper case, from a closed set of four. The handler names all four when it refuses. Bounded at 200 characters for the reason `reviewer` records.

family.description: Which finding family to read. **Refused rather than matched in this build**: no source `theurian findings build` reads derives a family, so every row's column is `null` and a filter on it answered `count: 0` for every value — an absence a caller reads as "nothing was recorded" (ADR-0029 D5). The refusal is one build constant, and it is a handler refusal rather than a schema one because a field withdrawn from the contract could not come back without a wire break, while a field that refuses can start working.

specialist.description: Which specialist's findings to read. Refused rather than matched in this build, for the reason `family` records, and published for the same one.

commitSha.description:
Which commit's findings to read: a full sha, 40 or 64 lower-case hex characters, as `git log --format=%H` prints it.

No published `pattern`. A short sha would match no row, and the handler refuses it with that sentence — a schema pattern would answer "does not satisfy" instead, and an empty answer read as "no findings on that commit" is exactly what the refusal exists to prevent.

pullRequest.description:
Which pull request's findings to read. Refused rather than matched in this build, for the reason `family` records.

No published `minimum` or `maximum`, although the column behind it is a signed 64-bit integer and the handler refuses anything outside it. That bound is checked before the inert-axis refusal fires, deliberately: a number the column cannot hold has a different thing wrong with it than an axis nothing derives, and it is the one a caller could act on if the axis is ever derived. A range here would leave that guard reachable by no request.

q.description: Free text to match against the finding line. Bounded at 200 characters for the reason `reviewer` records; an empty string is refused by the handler, because it matches nothing rather than everything.

limit.description:
How many findings to return. Defaults to 20, and the ceiling is a **refusal** rather than a clamp: this tool answers a filtered question with no paging, so a silently truncated page reads as "these are the findings matching my filter" when it is not (`theurian.mcp.findings.MAX_FINDINGS_LIMIT`). A page that does end early says so, through the response's `truncated`.

No published `minimum` or `maximum`: the handler's refusal names both ends and says why it is not a clamp, and a range here would answer "does not satisfy" in its place. `knowledge.search` clamps instead, and its own schema records why the two differ.
